title: Grade 6 Science — Thu, Jun 12
description: Separation of Substances — Day 4 of 5: Chromatography and magnetic separation
subject: science

questions.question: Chromatography is used to separate:
options: Different coloured dyes or inks mixed together
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates different dyes or pigments that are mixed together based on how fast they travel through a medium.

questions.question: In paper chromatography, the substance that moves up the paper is carried by:
questions.explanation: In paper chromatography, a liquid solvent (mobile phase) soaks up the paper and carries dissolved dye components upward.

questions.question: In a paper chromatography experiment with black ink, you often see:
options: Several separated colour bands (e.g., blue, red, yellow)
questions.explanation: Black ink is a mixture of several dyes. Chromatography separates them into coloured bands as different dyes travel different distances.

questions.question: The dye that travels farthest up the paper in chromatography is:
options: The most soluble dye (attracted least to paper)
questions.explanation: A dye that is very soluble in the solvent moves with it and travels far. A dye that clings to paper stays near the bottom.

questions.question: Chromatography is used in forensic science to:
options: Identify substances like inks, poisons, or drugs in crime scene samples
questions.explanation: Forensic scientists use chromatography to identify unknown substances (dyes, drugs, poisons) by comparing their chromatograms.

questions.question: Magnetic separation is used when one substance in a mixture is:
questions.explanation: If one substance is magnetic (iron, nickel, cobalt), a magnet can pull it out from a non-magnetic mixture.

questions.question: Iron filings mixed with sand can be separated using:
questions.explanation: A magnet attracts iron filings (which are magnetic) and pulls them away from sand (which is non-magnetic).

questions.question: In which industry is magnetic separation commonly used?
options: Coal and iron ore mining and processing
questions.explanation: In mining and recycling, magnetic separation removes iron and steel from other materials on conveyor belts.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is NOT attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is not magnetic. Only iron, nickel, cobalt, and some alloys are attracted by ordinary magnets.

questions.question: Chromatography can tell us if a food dye is pure or a mixture by:
options: Showing one spot (pure) or multiple spots/bands (mixture)
questions.explanation: A pure substance shows one spot in chromatography. A mixture separates into two or more spots or bands.

questions.question: A recycling plant uses a large magnet on a conveyor belt to separate:
options: Iron and steel cans from aluminium and plastic
questions.explanation: Steel (iron alloy) cans are magnetic and can be sorted from non-magnetic materials like aluminium and plastic using magnets.

questions.question: The word 'chromatography' comes from Greek words meaning:
questions.explanation: Chromatography = 'chroma' (colour) + 'graphe' (writing). It was first used to separate plant pigments (colours).

questions.question: In addition to paper, chromatography can also be done using:
options: Thin-layer (silica plate), gas, or liquid column chromatography
questions.explanation: Modern chromatography includes thin-layer chromatography (TLC), gas chromatography (GC), and column chromatography.

questions.question: Which separation method would you choose to separate iron nails from a mixture with plastic beads?
questions.explanation: Iron nails are magnetic; plastic beads are not. A magnet quickly separates them without any liquid or heat needed.

questions.question: Pigments in leaves can be separated using paper chromatography to show:
options: Multiple pigments like green chlorophyll, yellow xanthophyll, and orange carotene
Only the colour of the leaf
questions.explanation: Leaf chromatography reveals that leaves contain multiple pigments (green, yellow, orange) — not just green chlorophyll.
